title: Server-sent events: resume the cursor without hidden gaps
requiredVisibleLabel: Training rehearsal - synthetic data - not a live Azure result
objective: Resume a saved SSE event cursor and verify complete, ordered, exactly-once user-visible delivery against the original synthetic silence and recovery budget, not just a newly opened stream.
preconditions: A browser with standard local HTML, CSS and JavaScript; no server or account.
The old stream rendered evt-amber, evt-birch and evt-cedar in that order.
The declared remaining fixture is evt-delta, evt-elm and evt-fir; IDs are opaque.
Synthetic time zero is the last old user-visible event; the original clock never restarts at stream-open.
actions: Choose a saved, stale or absent cursor, bounded stream condition, replay policy and timing.
Start the old stream, cut over, then resume the SSE cursor.
Inspect stream establishment separately from missing, duplicate, reordered or unverified events and budget checks.
Check a prediction without changing the user outcome.
Start another attempt while retaining results, or explicitly reset all defaults and history.
assertions: Saved Last-Event-ID resumes strictly after the last rendered event.
A successful new stream with an expired replay window or tail-only cursor still fails completeness.
Wire replays are distinct from duplicate visible events; suppressed replay processing still consumes time.
Reordering fails even if the complete set of IDs is present.
First visible silence and total recovery are measured from the original last event; equality passes.
Incomplete observation remains unknown, unless a known failure already establishes interruption.
Input and state guards prevent silent advancement, history pruning and active configuration mutation.

iac.decisionStage: After genuine loadable-stub behavioral RED and before implementation.
iac.reason: Resource-free local synthetic lesson; no infrastructure, identity registration, cloud, deployment or expenditure is authorized.

limits: All IDs, data, events and elapsed times are deterministic synthetic fixtures.
No actual EventSource, SSE server, transport migration, Azure calls or live latency measurements.
No identities, tokens, keys or credentials are required or introduced.
Deduplication covers only this fixed six-ID in-memory fixture, not a general exactly-once SSE guarantee.
History lasts until explicit reset or page reload; it is bounded and never silently pruned.
B-S046 and D-S046 native/source-parent acceptance remain separate and unfulfilled.
One frozen S unit; tests, plumbing and evidence do not earn additional completion credit.
